findings.title: Technical language makes the service sound unnecessarily complicated
findings.evidence: “Leverage our multimodal generative narrative engine to synthesise bespoke, heirloom-grade story artefacts from your household's lived-experience corpus.”
findings.why: Several words are harder to understand than they need to be, which makes a warm family product feel corporate and less trustworthy.

findings.title: Proceed does not say whether login is required
findings.evidence: The primary button is labelled only “Proceed →” while a separate “Log in” link is in the header.
findings.why: I am not sure whether Proceed will take me to my account or begin a new process.

findings.title: Hero illustration has no accessible description
findings.evidence: The image is exposed as “[image (no description)]”.
findings.why: I cannot tell what the illustration depicts, and assistive technology users would miss that context.

findings.title: Login fields have placeholders instead of proper visible labels
findings.evidence: [5] and [6] are described as “textbox (no label)” with placeholders “Email” and “Password”
findings.why: Once I start typing, especially in the password field, the field can become harder to identify, and the form is less accessible.

findings.title: No visible password recovery option
findings.evidence: The page offers “Log in” and “Create an account” but no “Forgot password?” link.
findings.why: If I forget the password, there is no obvious way to recover the account from this page.

findings.title: Footer links have very low contrast
findings.evidence: In the screenshot, “Privacy”, “Terms”, “Contact”, and “© 2026 StoryHearth Ltd.” appear extremely faint against the pale background.
findings.why: I can hardly read or notice these links, so they look unavailable.

findings.title: Unexplained technical sync error
findings.evidence: “Error 0x80070057: profile sync incomplete.”
findings.why: I cannot tell whether it is safe to continue or whether some of my family details may be missing from the book.

findings.title: No explanation of sync consequences
findings.evidence: The warning only says “profile sync incomplete.”
findings.why: I do not know which details are affected or whether my new book may use incorrect information.

findings.title: No appearance field for the second character
findings.evidence: The page asks 'What do they look like? (optional)' only under the child's details, then moves straight to 'Who else is in the story?'
findings.why: I want the book to show Grandpa Joe with his grey hair, but I cannot enter that detail here.

findings.title: Footer text has very low contrast
findings.evidence: The footer shows 'Privacy', 'Terms', 'Contact' and '© 2026 StoryHearth Ltd.' in extremely faint text.
findings.why: I can barely see the privacy and contact links, so they look unavailable.

findings.title: No way to provide Grandpa Joe's appearance
findings.evidence: After asking "Who else is in the story?" and accepting "Grandpa Joe," this screen only offers "Where does the story happen?", "A special object", and "Tell us the memory or idea behind your story".
findings.why: I want Grandpa Joe to be recognisable in a book for Sam, and his grey hair is an important detail I know but cannot enter here.

findings.title: Reading-level jargon is unexplained
findings.evidence: The heading says “Reading level”, but every option is labelled with Lexile ranges such as [21] “Lexile BR–200L” and [22] “Lexile 200L–500L”.
findings.why: I do not know what Lexile means, so I cannot be confident that the book will actually suit a child aged five.

findings.title: No personal age-based recommendation
findings.evidence: Sam is age 5, but the page still has [22] “Lexile 200L–500L” selected and does not indicate that this may be too advanced.
findings.why: I would have to work out the reading level myself rather than trusting the site to use the age I already entered.

findings.title: The memory was silently truncated
findings.evidence: The result of entering field [18] said: “the box now only shows 200 characters; the end of what you typed was cut off”.
findings.why: I gave important details about Sam, Grandpa Joe’s grey hair, and the beach memory, but the site allowed a longer entry and then cut it off without warning.

findings.title: File control lacks a specific visible label
findings.evidence: [30] file-upload (no label) and “Choose file | No file chosen”
findings.why: Although the paragraph above explains that this is Sam’s photo, the upload control itself has no accessible or visible field label.

findings.title: Photo privacy and deletion are not explained
findings.evidence: “Upload a clear photo of your child's face so the illustrations look like them.”
findings.why: If I did upload a child’s photo, I would want to know how it is used, stored, and deleted before sharing it.

findings.title: Loading state has no explanatory status
findings.evidence: A circular loading spinner is shown by itself inside the central panel, with no accompanying text.
findings.why: I cannot tell whether the site is working, how long it may take, or whether my submission succeeded.

findings.title: No way to stop or leave while processing
findings.evidence: The central panel contains only the spinner, with no visible Cancel, Back, or edit control.
findings.why: If it gets stuck, I feel trapped and may refresh or give up.

findings.title: Generated title contains a spelling error
findings.evidence: “The Magical Adventrue of Sam”
findings.why: It looks unprofessional and makes me doubt whether the book was generated carefully.

findings.title: Illustration style appears not to match my selection
findings.evidence: The page says “Illustration style: Pop-art comic” even though I selected the Watercolour illustration style.
findings.why: I chose the appearance specifically, so this makes me wonder whether other choices were ignored too.

findings.title: No explanation of generation or choices applied
findings.evidence: The page changes from an unexplained loading state directly to the preview and only shows “Illustration style: Pop-art comic.”
findings.why: I cannot tell whether the book used all of my memory details or selected settings.

findings.title: Final page has an incomplete sentence
findings.evidence: “And from that day on, whenever Sam looked up at the sky, she would always remember”
findings.why: It makes the storybook feel broken rather than finished, especially for a five-year-old.

findings.title: Premium gift wrap is pre-selected
findings.evidence: [6] checkbox "Premium gift wrap" (checked), with “£7.99” underneath
findings.why: I might accidentally pay £7.97 more than the basic hardcover and shipping cost because I did not ask for gift wrap.

findings.title: Basic price is not obvious next to the total
findings.evidence: “Hardcover: The Magical Adventrue of Sam £24.99”, “Shipping & handling £12.99”, “Total £45.97”
findings.why: I can work out the £37.98 basic book-plus-shipping cost, but the page does not clearly show that subtotal separately from the add-on.

findings.title: Payment form asks for sensitive information before order review
findings.evidence: The visible form includes “Card number”, “Expiry”, and “CVC”, followed by a “Pay now” button.
findings.why: I need to inspect the price first and do not want to enter payment information in this study.

findings.title: Unclear time-limited price reservation
findings.evidence: “Your price is reserved for 09:46”
findings.why: The countdown makes me feel pressured to buy quickly, but it is unclear whether this is a countdown, a time limit, or merely the time remaining in a session.

findings.title: language
findings.evidence: The title says "The Magical Adventrue of Sam"; "Adventure" is misspelled as "Adventrue."

findings.title: fidelity
findings.evidence: The cover shows only Sam and a generic shoreline, with no Grandpa Joe, yellow bucket, sandcastles, or shared activity.

findings.title: visual_quality
findings.evidence: The image is very sparse and resembles a simple vector placeholder rather than a polished pop-art comic, despite the label "Illustration style: Pop-art comic."

findings.title: language
findings.evidence: The page visibly contains "{{recipient_name}}" and "{{sender_name}}" instead of names.

findings.title: fidelity
findings.evidence: No recipient or sender was supplied, yet the site has not removed or safely adapted the dedication fields.

findings.title: language
findings.evidence: The surrounding preview heading again shows "The Magical Adventrue of Sam."

findings.title: fidelity
findings.evidence: "Grandpa Joe" is absent, and the requested event of Sam and Grandpa Joe building sandcastles together never begins.

findings.title: language
findings.evidence: "in the beach" is ungrammatical; standard wording is "at the beach."

findings.title: text_image_fit
findings.evidence: The text says Sam loves a yellow bucket, but no yellow bucket appears in I3.

findings.title: character_consistency
findings.evidence: The child has short brown hair, but the plain green shirt and trousers do not clearly establish Sam as a girl despite the requested "she/her" pronouns.

findings.title: age_fit
findings.evidence: The sentence uses "ephemeral," "luminescence," "crepuscular firmament," "engendered," "melancholy," "juxtaposing," "ineffable," and "existential trepidation." The measured grade level was 6.9 rather than the requested age 5 level.

findings.title: fidelity
findings.evidence: The supplied memory was a "happy day" involving Grandpa Joe, laughter, and working together, not a solitary evening filled with melancholy.

findings.title: coherence
findings.evidence: The story changes from a sunny beach introduction to "One evening" without explaining what happened in between.

findings.title: text_image_fit
findings.evidence: The sky and evening colours broadly fit the text, but Sam is standing straight ahead rather than "gazed upward," and I4 contains a dark blocky artefact near the sun.

findings.title: language
findings.evidence: The story spells Sam's name as "Samn."

findings.title: text_image_fit
findings.evidence: The text describes pouring rain, grey drops, puddles, and a hood, while I5 shows a bright sun, no rain, no puddles, and no hood.

findings.title: fidelity
findings.evidence: Although the yellow bucket is mentioned, it is not illustrated, and Grandpa Joe and the sandcastle-building memory remain absent.

findings.title: coherence
findings.evidence: Sam runs away from the beach without the trusted adult requested in the story, beginning a sudden and unexplained adventure.

findings.title: fidelity
findings.evidence: The requested relative, "Grandpa Joe," is replaced by the invented character "Uncle Bartholomew."

findings.title: language
findings.evidence: "Sam, follow me!" he called, and he followed him along the winding path" leaves the pronoun references unclear and sounds as though Uncle Bartholomew may be following Sam.

findings.title: coherence
findings.evidence: Uncle Bartholomew appears suddenly and redirects Sam away from the beach without a clear connection to the previous event.

findings.title: text_image_fit
findings.evidence: I6 includes Bartholomew and a possible lantern, but the surrounding image is still the beach and does not show the stated winding path.

findings.title: age_fit
findings.evidence: "The shadows grew teeth" and "no one would ever find Sam again" introduce a threatening, disappearance-related fantasy that may be too frightening for a five-year-old.

findings.title: coherence
findings.evidence: The story jumps from a beach and winding path to "Deep in the woods" without establishing why Sam went there or how the trusted adult would respond.

findings.title: fidelity
findings.evidence: The red balloon and threatening woods are invented, while Grandpa Joe, the sandcastles, the sea breeze, and the shared laughter are still missing.

findings.title: text_image_fit
findings.evidence: The night woods and red balloon fit generally, but I7 does not show teeth on the shadows or indicate that they are whispering.

findings.title: coherence
findings.evidence: "Once upon a time, in the beach, there lived a curious child named Sam" repeats the opening after Sam has already left the beach and entered the woods.

findings.title: fidelity
findings.evidence: The supposedly happy ending does not mention Grandpa Joe, their sandcastles, the yellow bucket, Grandpa's sandy grey hair, or the laughter and teamwork supplied in the memory.

findings.title: text_image_fit
findings.evidence: The text says Sam "skipped all the way home," but the image shows her standing still in the same generic shoreline scene used earlier.

findings.title: language
findings.evidence: The phrase "in the beach" is repeated, and "the sun came out" is not connected to the earlier unexplained rain.

findings.title: language
findings.evidence: The sentence ends at "she would always remember" with no object or final punctuation, and "The End" appears both before and after the unfinished sentence.

findings.title: coherence
findings.evidence: The intended final memory is incomplete, so the story does not provide a clear emotional resolution.

findings.title: fidelity
findings.evidence: The final sentence never identifies what Sam remembered, losing the central detail that she remembered laughing and working together with Grandpa Joe.

findings.title: text_image_fit
findings.evidence: I9 matches the standalone "The End" label, but it shows neither Grandpa Joe nor sandcastles and does not illustrate Sam remembering the day.

findings.title: emotional_resonance
findings.evidence: A solitary placeholder figure and an incomplete sentence do not create a personal or keepsake-worthy closing moment.

findings.title: fidelity
findings.evidence: Premium gift wrap was selected, but its checkbox appears empty and the £37.98 total equals only £24.99 plus £12.99 shipping, excluding the £7.99 gift wrap.

findings.title: language
findings.evidence: Checkout repeats "The Magical Adventrue of Sam," and the arithmetic is inconsistent: £24.99 + £7.99 + £12.99 equals £45.97, not £37.98.

findings.title: visual_quality
findings.evidence: The checkout layout is clean, but the selected-option state and total are unclear, which creates a risk of charging for the wrong configuration.

findings.title: input fidelity: missing
findings.evidence: Grandpa Joe appears zero times and is not illustrated.

findings.title: input fidelity: missing
findings.evidence: Building sandcastles together is missing.

findings.title: input fidelity: missing
findings.evidence: Grandpa Joe's grey hair getting sandy is missing.

findings.title: input fidelity: missing
findings.evidence: The sea breeze is missing.

findings.title: input fidelity: missing
findings.evidence: Sam laughing and working together with Grandpa Joe is missing.

findings.title: input fidelity: missing
findings.evidence: The central happy-day memory is not carried through.

findings.title: input fidelity: missing
findings.evidence: The requested BR–200L reading level is not met; the measured grade level is 6.9.

findings.title: input fidelity: missing
findings.evidence: The selected premium gift wrap is not correctly reflected in the checkout state or total.

findings.title: input fidelity: changed
findings.evidence: The requested happy family beach day was changed into a sombre fantasy adventure.

findings.title: input fidelity: changed
findings.evidence: The trusted family relationship with Grandpa Joe was omitted.

findings.title: input fidelity: changed
findings.evidence: The plain-vector artwork is described as "Pop-art comic" but is not developed as a comic-style sequence.

findings.title: input fidelity: changed
findings.evidence: The requested gift-wrap configuration appears to have been dropped at checkout.

findings.title: safety concern
findings.evidence: The toothy shadows whispering that no one would ever find Sam, followed by Sam trembling alone in the dark woods, may be frightening for a five-year-old, particularly because Grandpa Joe is absent from the threatening sequence.
